name: Zams
kurzbeschreibung: Charming market town at the entrance to the Stanzer Tal valley, featuring a late Gothic parish church and the Zams-Schönwies ski area.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The municipality of Zams lies at 767 metres above sea level in the sunny Landeck valley basin in the Tyrolean Oberland, within the district of Landeck. It extends along the confluence of the Sanna and Inn rivers, directly across from the district capital of Landeck and at the foot of the Venet mountain massif with its 2,208-metre peak, the Krahberg. Home to around 3,540 residents, Zams covers an extensive territory reaching deep into the Lechtal Alps. Positioned at the crossroads of major alpine transit corridors into the Stanzer Valley, Paznaun, Kaunertal, and southwards via the Reschen Pass into South Tyrol and Switzerland, Zams blends rich history with dramatic mountain scenery.

Geschichte

During Roman antiquity, the Via Claudia Augusta passed through the basin. Zams was first documented in 1150 as Zamis. The town's historical development is closely tied to the Sisters of Mercy of St. Vincent de Paul, who established their motherhouse here in 1826 along with St. Vincent Hospital, which remains the principal medical centre for the Tyrolean Oberland. A defining tragedy took place on 11 August 1911, when a catastrophic fire consumed almost the entire village, destroying 45 homes and the parish church. The Gothic bell tower miraculously survived. When the new parish church of St. Andrew was rebuilt in 1912 on a slightly shifted site, the old tower was left standing completely detached in the village centre—a striking freestanding campanile. Perched above the river Inn also stand the 14th-century Kronburg castle ruins and pilgrimage church.

Anreise

Zams features outstanding transport connections. Motorists reach the town directly via the Inntal motorway A12 and Arlberg expressway S16 at junction Landeck/Zams, alongside the federal highways B171 and B180 towards the Reschen Pass and Italy. The Landeck-Zams railway station is a major international stop along the Arlberg rail line, regularly served by Railjet, Eurocity, and Nightjet trains linking Vienna, Zurich, and Bregenz. From the station square, comprehensive regional bus services depart for all surrounding valleys including Paznaun, Arlberg, and Kaunertal.

Tipps

A premier attraction is the Zammer Lochputz, a mystical gorge featuring the thunderous Lötz waterfall, secure cliffside footbridges, a historic 1923 hydroelectric plant, and the medieval Mirror Tower with multimedia exhibits. The Venet cable car whisks visitors up to the Venet recreation mountain at 2,208 metres, offering a stunning 360-degree panorama across the Ötztal, Lechtal, and Silvretta ranges, celebrated by hikers and paragliders. Cultural visitors can walk to the scenic Kronburg ensemble, while long-distance hikers know Zams as a key staging post on the famous E5 alpine crossing from Oberstdorf to Merano.
